document.abstract: For many years there has been an emphasis on increasing dynamic range and color saturation in television and, to an even greater extent, in digital cinema. This begs the question; just how much data do we really need to record and store? An epic motion picture to be shown on a 20 m screen at 3000:1 contrast ratio could justify the ultimate image quality, but this could be overkill for a daily breakfast show typically viewed in a kitchen. This paper discusses aspects of studio production and image quality with regard to present day imagers and current market trends.
